name: reading-experience
description: Reusable browser-level check definitions for the five-story reading experience. Elara runs these as page checks against the loopback-only production server (npm start, http://127.0.0.1:3000). Every route is checked at each viewport: the skip-link keyboard flow, the server-rendered reading progress (exactly one aria-current link, the exact 'Story N of 5' position, the next-story cue or the story-five ending), the landmarks, evidence and citation rendering, and clean console, request and scroll behaviour. This file remains reusable browser-check definition data that Elara's page checks consume: the browser steps run only as Elara page checks. In the current design the wide top section (the hero) is the first element inside main#main-content, so the checks expect main#main-content h1, a review date inside main, and the opening illustration inside main. The recorded results of Elara's page checks are in docs/runbooks/accessibility-validation.md; this file is the definition data those checks consume, not a result log. npm run verify:reading (scripts/verify-reading.mjs) starts and stops its own loopback production server and checks the five server-rendered HTTP responses for the essential story content, local illustrations, citations, disclaimers, ordinary navigation links, and the correct current-page state, using the serverContract object below; it never executes page JavaScript and never launches a browser, and those checks are safeguards, not proof of complete no-JavaScript browser behaviour or WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.

serverContract.description: The server-rendered reading contract that scripts/verify-reading.mjs enforces over plain HTTP. The script starts and stops its own loopback production server (npm start), fetches all five routes without executing JavaScript or launching a browser, and checks each response: the wide top section (the hero) as the first element inside the single main#main-content (only whitespace between the main open tag and the hero open tag), with exactly one h1 (heading) and a review-date time with a non-empty datetime, exactly one main#main-content with a body paragraph, the title substrings in the document <title>, at least one local illustration (imageSrcPrefix) that answers HTTP 200 with an image content type with the page's opening illustration in the hero, at least one https:// citation anchor inside main, the visible disclaimer, the header nav with exactly the five story links in reading order, exactly one aria-current on this route's link, the 'Story N of 5' label, and the skip link before the header. Story 5 carries endingState and visibleStrings and no next-story link; stories 1 to 4 carry a next-story cue to the following route. Where this object is incomplete the script falls back to its built-in copy of the same contract, so the enforced contract never weakens.

unverifiedGaps.check: Skip-link flow, progress rendering, zoom, reflow and navigation in native Safari on macOS and iOS (the documented supported browser, not WebKit in general).
unverifiedGaps.note: WebKit is not native Safari: a WebKit-engine result is not represented here as native Safari coverage.

unverifiedGaps.check: Screen reader navigation: landmark and heading structure, the skip link, and the reading-progress cue announced correctly with assistive technology.
200% page zoom: content stays readable, the skip link still reaches main, and no sideways scrolling appears at or beyond the viewport widths above.
Reflow at viewport widths and aspect ratios beyond the listed widths (320, 375, 768, 1280, 1920 px).

JavaScript-off reading in a real browser: with JavaScript disabled, all five routes must show the story heading, the opening illustration, the citations, the 'not medical advice' disclaimer, the five navigation links, and the current-page state, and remain usable.
unverifiedGaps.note: npm run verify:reading is a Node-only loopback HTTP safeguard: it never executes page JavaScript and never launches a browser, so it is not a substitute for this check.

unverifiedGaps.check: In-browser accessibility audit (axe or Lighthouse) on each of the five routes.
unverifiedGaps.note: Run by a person in the browser (axe DevTools, the Lighthouse accessibility audit, or the developer-tools accessibility pane); no npm script launches axe, Lighthouse, or any browser automation.

unverifiedGaps.check: The dark theme in a real browser: the theme follows the reader's system setting via prefers-color-scheme (no theme switch, no JavaScript), and every route must be fully readable with the dark surfaces applied throughout, a visible focus outline, and no sideways scrolling.
unverifiedGaps.note: Elara's browser checks cannot switch the theme; a real browser with a dark system setting is the only way to observe the dark theme.

unverifiedGaps.check: Reduced-motion behaviour: with the reader's reduced-motion preference on, no motion must be visible and all content must stay fully visible and readable; with no preference, the decorative motion plays once, lasts under 5 seconds, never loops, and never carries required information.
unverifiedGaps.note: Elara's browser checks cannot change the reader's reduced-motion preference.

notes: Browser behaviour is exercised only by Elara page checks against the loopback production server; this file is data, not an executable test, and nothing in it runs under a Node script.

npm run verify:reading (scripts/verify-reading.mjs) is a Node-only loopback HTTP safeguard: it starts and stops its own loopback production server (npm start) and checks the five server-rendered HTTP responses for the essential story content, local illustrations, citations, disclaimers, ordinary navigation links, and the correct current-page state, using the serverContract object above. It never executes page JavaScript and never launches a browser, and its results are safeguards, not proof of complete no-JavaScript browser behaviour or WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
No unverified gap above is marked as passed, and browser behaviour is not a completed WCAG 2.2 AA or cross-browser verification claim.
